This program will also provide students with the opportunity to enter the neuroscience workforce with all the benefits of a master’s degree without losing the time and expenses that two years of traditional graduate study would otherwise cost them.

The goal of the program is for students to be able complete an accelerated bachelor to masters program within a five-year period.

The key players in the INP ABM program, namely the students, faculty, staff, will be striving to achieve one common purpose: to learn and lead together.
The ABM program also aligns with the current strategic plan by fostering student success, exposing students to cutting edge research and lab techniques, and by embracing diversity at both the student and faculty level.
It is important to note that the INP is committed to supporting the diversity of the neuroscience students and has a Standing Committee, the Diversity Initiative Committee, devoted to this effort.
Recent research regarding graduation trends in neuroscience supports that greater numbers of females are graduating from neuroscience bachelor’s and graduate degree programs.
White (non-Hispanic) males and females represent the largest group of graduates and Asian/Pacific Islanders represent the largest non-White group of graduates.
